domains.name: Fraud governance and accountability
domains.covers: Who is accountable for fraud risk, how the board, owners or group oversee it, the fraud and corruption policy and response plan, legal duties to report and prevent fraud and corruption, resourcing, assurance and fidelity insurance, governance of the organisation's own AI tools, and whether the programme measures itself and applies its lessons.
domains.opens: The organisation profile supplies who has final oversight, which legal regimes apply (the PFMA or MFMA, FICA, the Companies Act social and ethics requirement, or a financial institution or communications provider) and the organisation's size. Every organisation answers the accountability, policy, legal, resourcing, AI and improvement sections, and the oversight section follows the structure that actually exists.
ai: AI-enabled fraud, such as deepfake impersonation and forged documents, named in the fraud policy
Board or council briefing on AI-enabled threats
Knowing which AI tools people use, and keeping confidential data out of public tools
A named owner, a human check and a way to stop each AI tool that approves, pays, onboards or decides
Crime insurance that covers payments made on deepfake or impersonated instructions
Written limits on what each AI tool may decide without a person's approval

bank.name: Fraud governance and accountability
bank.status: Combined MK draft for content review

responseRules.applicability: A section opens when the activity it covers exists, as recorded in the organisation profile or the domain's opening questions. Organisation structure changes who answers and how questions are worded, not whether a control is examined.
responseRules.dependencies: A follow-up is hidden only when the answer it depends on makes it logically impossible, for example reviewing a register that does not exist. Each such follow-up records the reason. Independent controls are always asked.
responseRules.unknown: 'I don't know' assigns the question to the suggested owner. Anything that depends on that answer is held as pending for that owner; it is never treated as absent, present or not applicable.
responseRules.depth: Core questions give a short, comparable read of every domain. Detail questions are the full diagnostic. Both use the same answers, so a Core read can be extended later.
responseRules.scoring: No score, weighting or severity is calculated. Levels are ordered descriptions, not numbers, until MK approves a scoring method.
responseRules.relevance: Each question and section can carry a relevance rule built from the organisation profile: size, measured by headcount or turnover, and industry. The engine leaves out anything that is not relevant before the flow starts. Size leaves out controls that a small team cannot reasonably run; industry leaves out activities that are very unlikely in that industry. A question that depends on another inherits that question's relevance.

bank.scopeNote: Whether the organisation assesses its fraud risks, and if so who owns the assessment, what it covers, how schemes are identified and rated, whether they are matched to tested controls, whether the results are acted on, how the assessment is kept current, and whether it is documented and connected to other risk work.

responseRules.applicability: A section opens when the activity it covers exists, as recorded in the organisation profile or the domain's opening questions. Organisation structure changes who answers and how questions are worded, not whether a control is examined.
responseRules.dependencies: A follow-up is hidden only when the answer it depends on makes it logically impossible, for example reviewing a register that does not exist. Each such follow-up records the reason. Independent controls are always asked.
responseRules.unknown: 'I don't know' assigns the question to the suggested owner. Anything that depends on that answer is held as pending for that owner; it is never treated as absent, present or not applicable.
responseRules.depth: Core questions give a short, comparable read of every domain. Detail questions are the full diagnostic. Both use the same answers, so a Core read can be extended later.
responseRules.scoring: No score, weighting or severity is calculated. Levels are ordered descriptions, not numbers, until MK approves a scoring method.
responseRules.relevance: Each question and section can carry a relevance rule built from the organisation profile: size, measured by headcount or turnover, and industry. The engine leaves out anything that is not relevant before the flow starts. Size leaves out controls that a small team cannot reasonably run; industry leaves out activities that are very unlikely in that industry. A question that depends on another inherits that question's relevance.

responseRules.applicability: A section opens when the activity it covers exists, as recorded in the organisation profile or the domain's opening questions. Organisation structure changes who answers and how questions are worded, not whether a control is examined.
responseRules.dependencies: A follow-up is hidden only when the answer it depends on makes it logically impossible, for example reviewing a register that does not exist. Each such follow-up records the reason. Independent controls are always asked.
responseRules.unknown: 'I don't know' assigns the question to the suggested owner. Anything that depends on that answer is held as pending for that owner; it is never treated as absent, present or not applicable.
responseRules.depth: Core questions give a short, comparable read of every domain. Detail questions are the full diagnostic. Both use the same answers, so a Core read can be extended later.
responseRules.scoring: No score, weighting or severity is calculated. Levels are ordered descriptions, not numbers, until MK approves a scoring method.
responseRules.relevance: Each question and section can carry a relevance rule built from the organisation profile: size, measured by headcount or turnover, and industry. The engine leaves out anything that is not relevant before the flow starts. Size leaves out controls that a small team cannot reasonably run; industry leaves out activities that are very unlikely in that industry. A question that depends on another inherits that question's relevance.

responseRules.applicability: A section opens when the activity it covers exists, as recorded in the organisation profile or the domain's opening questions. Organisation structure changes who answers and how questions are worded, not whether a control is examined.
responseRules.dependencies: A follow-up is hidden only when the answer it depends on makes it logically impossible, for example reviewing a register that does not exist. Each such follow-up records the reason. Independent controls are always asked.
responseRules.unknown: 'I don't know' assigns the question to the suggested owner. Anything that depends on that answer is held as pending for that owner; it is never treated as absent, present or not applicable.
responseRules.depth: Core questions give a short, comparable read of every domain. Detail questions are the full diagnostic. Both use the same answers, so a Core read can be extended later.
responseRules.scoring: No score, weighting or severity is calculated. Levels are ordered descriptions, not numbers, until MK approves a scoring method.
responseRules.relevance: Each question and section can carry a relevance rule built from the organisation profile: size, measured by headcount or turnover, and industry. The engine leaves out anything that is not relevant before the flow starts. Size leaves out controls that a small team cannot reasonably run; industry leaves out activities that are very unlikely in that industry. A question that depends on another inherits that question's relevance.

responseRules.applicability: A section opens when the activity it covers exists, as recorded in the organisation profile or the domain's opening questions. Organisation structure changes who answers and how questions are worded, not whether a control is examined.
responseRules.dependencies: A follow-up is hidden only when the answer it depends on makes it logically impossible, for example reviewing a register that does not exist. Each such follow-up records the reason. Independent controls are always asked.
responseRules.unknown: 'I don't know' assigns the question to the suggested owner. Anything that depends on that answer is held as pending for that owner; it is never treated as absent, present or not applicable.
responseRules.depth: Core questions give a short, comparable read of every domain. Detail questions are the full diagnostic. Both use the same answers, so a Core read can be extended later.
responseRules.scoring: No score, weighting or severity is calculated. Levels are ordered descriptions, not numbers, until MK approves a scoring method.
responseRules.relevance: Each question and section can carry a relevance rule built from the organisation profile: size, measured by headcount or turnover, and industry. The engine leaves out anything that is not relevant before the flow starts. Size leaves out controls that a small team cannot reasonably run; industry leaves out activities that are very unlikely in that industry. A question that depends on another inherits that question's relevance.

responseRules.applicability: A section opens when the activity it covers exists, as recorded in the organisation profile or the domain's opening questions. Organisation structure changes who answers and how questions are worded, not whether a control is examined.
responseRules.dependencies: A follow-up is hidden only when the answer it depends on makes it logically impossible, for example reviewing a register that does not exist. Each such follow-up records the reason. Independent controls are always asked.
responseRules.unknown: 'I don't know' assigns the question to the suggested owner. Anything that depends on that answer is held as pending for that owner; it is never treated as absent, present or not applicable.
responseRules.depth: Core questions give a short, comparable read of every domain. Detail questions are the full diagnostic. Both use the same answers, so a Core read can be extended later.
responseRules.scoring: No score, weighting or severity is calculated. Levels are ordered descriptions, not numbers, until MK approves a scoring method.
responseRules.relevance: Each question and section can carry a relevance rule built from the organisation profile: size, measured by headcount or turnover, and industry. The engine leaves out anything that is not relevant before the flow starts. Size leaves out controls that a small team cannot reasonably run; industry leaves out activities that are very unlikely in that industry. A question that depends on another inherits that question's relevance.

responseRules.applicability: A section opens when the activity it covers exists, as recorded in the organisation profile or the domain's opening questions. Organisation structure changes who answers and how questions are worded, not whether a control is examined.
responseRules.dependencies: A follow-up is hidden only when the answer it depends on makes it logically impossible, for example reviewing a register that does not exist. Each such follow-up records the reason. Independent controls are always asked.
responseRules.unknown: 'I don't know' assigns the question to the suggested owner. Anything that depends on that answer is held as pending for that owner; it is never treated as absent, present or not applicable.
responseRules.depth: Core questions give a short, comparable read of every domain. Detail questions are the full diagnostic. Both use the same answers, so a Core read can be extended later.
responseRules.scoring: No score, weighting or severity is calculated. Levels are ordered descriptions, not numbers, until MK approves a scoring method.
responseRules.relevance: Each question and section can carry a relevance rule built from the organisation profile: size, measured by headcount or turnover, and industry. The engine leaves out anything that is not relevant before the flow starts. Size leaves out controls that a small team cannot reasonably run; industry leaves out activities that are very unlikely in that industry. A question that depends on another inherits that question's relevance.

responseRules.applicability: A section opens when the activity it covers exists, as recorded in the organisation profile or the domain's opening questions. Organisation structure changes who answers and how questions are worded, not whether a control is examined.
responseRules.dependencies: A follow-up is hidden only when the answer it depends on makes it logically impossible, for example reviewing a register that does not exist. Each such follow-up records the reason. Independent controls are always asked.
responseRules.unknown: 'I don't know' assigns the question to the suggested owner. Anything that depends on that answer is held as pending for that owner; it is never treated as absent, present or not applicable.
responseRules.depth: Core questions give a short, comparable read of every domain. Detail questions are the full diagnostic. Both use the same answers, so a Core read can be extended later.
responseRules.scoring: No score, weighting or severity is calculated. Levels are ordered descriptions, not numbers, until MK approves a scoring method.
responseRules.relevance: Each question and section can carry a relevance rule built from the organisation profile: size, measured by headcount or turnover, and industry. The engine leaves out anything that is not relevant before the flow starts. Size leaves out controls that a small team cannot reasonably run; industry leaves out activities that are very unlikely in that industry. A question that depends on another inherits that question's relevance.

responseScale.label: Not in place

responseScale.label: Informal / reactive

responseScale.label: Partly designed
responseScale.meaning: The practice is partly designed; important elements are missing or inconsistent.

responseScale.label: Implemented in key areas
responseScale.meaning: The practice works in the key areas, but not yet across the whole organisation.

responseScale.label: Consistently operating
responseScale.meaning: The practice is defined, works consistently and could be shown with evidence.

responseScale.label: Embedded and improving
responseScale.meaning: The practice is measured, governed and deliberately improved over time.

Payment release controls are covered in D6 and remote customer onboarding in D7.

responseRules.applicability: A section opens when the activity it covers exists, as recorded in the organisation profile or the domain's opening questions. Organisation structure changes who answers and how questions are worded, not whether a control is examined.
responseRules.dependencies: A follow-up is hidden only when the answer it depends on makes it logically impossible, for example reviewing a register that does not exist. Each such follow-up records the reason. Independent controls are always asked.
responseRules.unknown: 'I don't know' assigns the question to the suggested owner. Anything that depends on that answer is held as pending for that owner; it is never treated as absent, present or not applicable.
responseRules.depth: Core questions give a short, comparable read of every domain. Detail questions are the full diagnostic. Both use the same answers, so a Core read can be extended later.
responseRules.scoring: No score, weighting or severity is calculated. Levels are ordered descriptions, not numbers, until MK approves a scoring method.
responseRules.relevance: Each question and section can carry a relevance rule built from the organisation profile: size, measured by headcount or turnover, and industry. The engine leaves out anything that is not relevant before the flow starts. Size leaves out controls that a small team cannot reasonably run; industry leaves out activities that are very unlikely in that industry. A question that depends on another inherits that question's relevance.

responseScale.label: Embedded and improving
responseScale.meaning: The practice is measured, governed and deliberately improved over time.

responseRules.applicability: A section opens when the activity it covers exists, as recorded in the organisation profile or the domain's opening questions. Organisation structure changes who answers and how questions are worded, not whether a control is examined.
responseRules.dependencies: A follow-up is hidden only when the answer it depends on makes it logically impossible, for example reviewing a register that does not exist. Each such follow-up records the reason. Independent controls are always asked.
responseRules.unknown: 'I don't know' assigns the question to the suggested owner. Anything that depends on that answer is held as pending for that owner; it is never treated as absent, present or not applicable.
responseRules.depth: Core questions give a short, comparable read of every domain. Detail questions are the full diagnostic. Both use the same answers, so a Core read can be extended later.
responseRules.scoring: No score, weighting or severity is calculated. Levels are ordered descriptions, not numbers, until MK approves a scoring method.
responseRules.relevance: Each question and section can carry a relevance rule built from the organisation profile: size, measured by headcount or turnover, and industry. The engine leaves out anything that is not relevant before the flow starts. Size leaves out controls that a small team cannot reasonably run; industry leaves out activities that are very unlikely in that industry. A question that depends on another inherits that question's relevance.

responseScale.label: Not in place
responseScale.meaning: The practice is absent or is not recognised as needed.

responseScale.label: Informal / reactive
responseScale.meaning: Something happens, but informally, after the fact or only through individual effort.

responseScale.label: Partly designed
responseScale.meaning: The practice is partly designed; important elements are missing or inconsistent.

responseScale.label: Implemented in key areas
responseScale.meaning: The practice works in the key areas, but not yet across the whole organisation.

responseScale.label: Consistently operating
responseScale.meaning: The practice is defined, works consistently and could be shown with evidence.

responseScale.label: Embedded and improving
responseScale.meaning: The practice is measured, governed and deliberately improved over time.
